focus: Middle-end and backend: DataFlowAnalysis stage (SSA + expression building) -> Typing/Type Reconstruction -> Structure Analysis (CFG->AST) -> Output (code emission)

pipeline.name: Interprocedural Analysis via SCC
pipeline.description: Finds strongly connected components (SCCs) in the call graph using bottom-up topological order. Each SCC is processed as an atomic unit to enable interprocedural analysis of preserved/trashed registers and parameter usage across recursive/mutually-recursive procedures.
pipeline.outputs: ProgramDataFlow (per-procedure signature summaries, preserved/trashed registers, live-in/live-out registers)
substeps: per-SCC: CreateSccWorker(procs).Transform() - orchestrate all transforms for that SCC

pipeline.name: SSA Transformation per SCC
pipeline.description: For each procedure in SCC: convert to SSA form while handling calls to already-visited procedures (via ProcedureFlow) or unvisited/computed calls (hell nodes). Handles register aliasing, stack-based frame variables, indirect calls iteratively.
pipeline.inputs: Procedure CFG in low-level form (assignments, calls with implicit register uses/defs)
pipeline.outputs: SsaState (SSA identifiers, phi functions, exception nodes)
substeps: ConvertToSsa per proc (lines 160-277): creates SsaTransform, runs ~15 sub-transforms in sequence
- IndirectCallRewriter loop [lines 235-240]: repeats while changes found
ValuePropagator + SsaTransform loop [lines 113-118] for stack variables

pipeline.name: Expression Building (Post-SSA)
pipeline.description: Per procedure (after all SCCs): apply expression coalescing, induction variable analysis, web building to convert low-level SSA into expression trees. Fixed-point iterations of ValuePropagator + Coalescer.
pipeline.outputs: High-level expression trees (phi webs, coalesced identifiers)
substeps: UnSsaTransform(false) [converts SSA back to quasi-single-assignment form]

pipeline.name: Type Collection & Equivalence Class Building
pipeline.description: Per program: collect data types from instructions and signatures, build equivalence classes of expressions that must have the same type via type variable unification.
pipeline.inputs: Program with typed procedures, expressions in SSA form
pipeline.outputs: TypeStore with equivalence classes, TypeVariables unified
substeps: EquivalenceClassBuilder.Build(program) - assign type variables to each expr, collect constraints
TypeCollector.CollectTypes() - walk all instructions, meet/join types from uses and defs

pipeline.name: Type Inference & Reconstruction
pipeline.description: Per program: unify type variables, transform to concrete data types, inline structures, replace primitive-typed pointers, reconstruct complex types (structs, arrays), rewrite program expressions with inferred types.
pipeline.outputs: Program with TypedExpressions (casts applied, field accesses instead of memory ops), Type declarations
substeps: PtrPrimitiveReplacer.ReplaceAll() - upgrade primitive ptrs to typed ptrs
TypeTransformer.Transform() - apply inlining, complex type naming rules
TypedExpressionRewriter.RewriteProgram() - rewrite ssa procedure statements with types

pipeline.name: Control Flow Structuring (CFG -> Regions)
pipeline.description: Per procedure: convert flat CFG (blocks+jumps) into hierarchical regions (sequences, if-then-else, switches, loops) via iterative refinement, emitting high-level AbsynStatement trees.
pipeline.outputs: Procedure.Body (list of AbsynStatement: AbsynIf, AbsynLoop, AbsynSwitch, etc.)
substeps: CompoundConditionCoalescer.Transform() - merge adjacent branches into compound conditions
RegionGraphBuilder.Build() - convert CFG blocks to Region hierarchy
Iterative structuring loop until no more reductions (lines 143-186):
Post-order DFS traversal of region graph
ReduceAcyclic(region): match and reduce if/switch/sequence patterns [lines 241-263]
ReduceCyclic(region): match and reduce loop patterns if not acyclic
ProcessUnresolvedRegions(): refinement queue for unstructured cases [lines 279-308]
- VirtualizeReturn: insert return statements to break cycles
- RefineIncSwitch(switchHead): virtualize edges to normalize switch pattern
- LastResort: insert goto nodes when stuck
IfCascadeToSwitchRewriter - convert if-else chains to switch
ForLoopRewriter - recognize for loops from while

pipeline.name: Absyn Statement Emission
pipeline.description: Convert Region hierarchy and Procedure.Body to text output via formatters. Decisions: indentation, casts insertion, operator precedence.

feedback_loops.name: ValuePropagator + SsaTransform loop (indirect call resolution)
feedback_loops.trigger: IndirectCallRewriter.Rewrite() returns true (new call targets resolved)
feedback_loops.mechanism: While loop: IndirectCallRewriter.Rewrite() [lines 235-240 in SccWorker.cs] calls vp.Transform() then sst.Transform() if changed

feedback_loops.name: ValuePropagator + ConditionCodeEliminator loop
feedback_loops.trigger: ConditionCodeEliminator uncovers more constant flags or condition patterns
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ValuePropagator to propagate newly-eliminated condition code uses

feedback_loops.name: Stack variable discovery + SSA rebuild
feedback_loops.trigger: ComplexStackVariableTransformer or StackPointerBackpropagator discovers new stack-based variables
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: SsaTransform with RenameFrameAccesses=true to re-SSA the new frame identifiers
feedback_loops.mechanism: SsaTransform.RenameFrameAccesses flag, called ~4 times after each frame-access-creating transform [lines 116, 231, 239, 259]

feedback_loops.name: Coalescer + ValuePropagator loop
feedback_loops.trigger: Coalescer subsumes definitions into uses, revealing new propagation opportunities
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ValuePropagator to fold constants and propagate coalesced values
feedback_loops.mechanism: Sequence with DeadCode in between: Coalescer [279-280] -> DeadCode -> ValuePropagator [283] in DataFlowAnalysis.BuildExpressionTrees()

feedback_loops.name: Region reduction loop until convergence
feedback_loops.trigger: Each iteration: ReduceAcyclic or ReduceCyclic succeeds, reducing region count, or ProcessUnresolvedRegions refines stuck regions
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Recompute DominatorGraph and re-traverse region graph in post-order
feedback_loops.mechanism: Outer do-while loop (lines 143-185): continues while regionGraph.Nodes.Count > 1; inner loop rebuilds doms per iteration

feedback_loops.name: Type equivalence class unification (implicit fixed-point in union-find)
feedback_loops.trigger: Each MeetDataType or EqualTrait adds constraints; union-find implicitly converges when all constraints processed
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Implied: re-traversal of constraints during BuildEquivalenceClassDataTypes or TypeTransformer, but not explicit restart
feedback_loops.mechanism: TypeStore uses union-find; constraints are one-pass; TypeTransformer may reveal inconsistencies but doesn't re-run type collection

feedback_loops.name: User-defined type constraints propagate backward through inference
feedback_loops.trigger: UserProcedure.Signature or UserGlobal.DataType provided in Program.User
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Type inference: TypeCollector honors user signatures via EnsureSignatureTypeVariables before per-instruction analysis
feedback_loops.mechanism: TypeCollector.EnsureSignatureTypeVariables() called per procedure [TypeCollector.cs:81-92] before instruction walk

decision_points.name: Heuristic: CallsRespectABI
decision_points.decision: Should implicit register uses/defs at call sites respect the platform ABI? If yes, use IsTrashedAbi; else use IsTrashedGuess heuristic.
decision_points.alternatives: If true: assume ABI-listed trashed registers are always killed by calls. If false: infer from data flow which registers are actually trashed by call targets.

decision_points.name: Heuristic: AggressiveBranchRemoval
decision_points.decision: Should UnreachableBlockRemover be run, aggressively removing blocks deemed unreachable? Default: false to preserve debug info.
decision_points.alternatives: If true: may remove blocks that confuse decompilers but may lose legitimate code. If false: preserve more conservative CFG.

decision_points.name: SCC vs. Single-Procedure Processing
decision_points.decision: Are procedures in same SCC processed together (allowing inter-SCC analysis of preserve/trash) or individually?
decision_points.alternatives: SCC-based (current): bottom-up, allows callees to inform callers' register summaries. Per-procedure: faster but loses interprocedural precision.

decision_points.name: When to stop region structuring iterations
decision_points.decision: Stop when regionGraph.Nodes.Count <= 1 OR iterations > 1000 (hardcoded timeout)
decision_points.alternatives: Max iterations could be user-configurable; could use progress heuristic (% reduction per iteration) to escape earlier.
decision_points.current_override: Hardcoded 1000 iteration limit; no configuration option

decision_points.name: Switch vs. Else-If Cascade
decision_points.decision: Convert long if-else chains into switch statements for readability?
decision_points.alternatives: If true: emit switch. If false: preserve cascading if-else (may be more faithful to original).
decision_points.current_override: Hardcoded: always run; no user control

decision_points.name: Type unification strictness in EquivalenceClassBuilder
decision_points.decision: How strict to be when unifying type variables? Allow unions of incompatible types, or fail?
decision_points.alternatives: Lenient: auto-widen to unions or void*. Strict: report error and skip.
decision_points.current_override: Determined by TypeTransformer rules; no explicit user override visible

decision_points.name: Expression simplification rules applied in ValuePropagator
decision_points.where: ExpressionSimplifier with ~30+ reduction rules (Add_mul_id_c_id_Rule, IdBinIdc_Rule, etc.)
decision_points.decision: Which algebraic simplification rules are active? (e.g., constant folding, strength reduction, slice coalescing)
decision_points.alternatives: All rules active (current). Could disable specific rules for preservation of original patterns.
decision_points.current_override: Hardcoded rule set instantiation; no configuration

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.User.Procedures (UserProcedure)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can specify procedure entry addresses, names, signatures, and calling conventions. These override inferred signatures.
intervention_surfaces.affects: SSA parameter/return identification, CallRewriter, type inference

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.User.Globals (UserGlobal)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can specify global variable addresses, names, and data types. Type system respects these.
intervention_surfaces.affects: Type collection, memory access rewriting, type inference

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.User.Calls (UserCallData)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can annotate call sites with target procedure or signature overrides.

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.User.Heuristics
intervention_surfaces.description: Set of string constants (e.g., 'aggressive-branch-removal', 'calls-respect-abi') to enable/disable analysis heuristics.

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.User.DebugTraceProcedures
intervention_surfaces.description: Set of procedure names to enable verbose debug output (DumpWatchedProcedure) for tracing specific procedures.
intervention_surfaces.affects: DataFlowAnalysis phase logging and test output generation

intervention_surfaces.name: IDecompilerEventListener.IsCanceled()
intervention_surfaces.description: Decompiler checks this at every major loop to allow user cancellation. User can implement to return true to abort.
intervention_surfaces.affects: All stages: SccWorker loops, TypeAnalyzer, StructureAnalysis, DataFlowAnalysis

intervention_surfaces.name: IAnalysisFactory.CreateSsaAnalyses(stage, ssa, context)
intervention_surfaces.description: Architecture-specific extension point: processors can register custom SSA analyses (e.g., x86-specific instruction patterns) at specified AnalysisStage.
intervention_surfaces.affects: BuildExpressionTrees and ConvertToSsa: RunAnalyses() calls this for AfterRegisterSsa, AfterExpressionCoalescing stages

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.NeedsSsaTransform
intervention_surfaces.description: Some IR formats (e.g., LLVM) already have SSA; flag controls whether SsaTransform is even called.

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.NeedsTypeReconstruction
intervention_surfaces.description: Some IR formats may have types already; flag controls whether TypeAnalyzer.RewriteProgram() is called.

intervention_surfaces.name: ExpressionSimplifier rule instances (static fields)
intervention_surfaces.description: The ~30 simplification rules in ExpressionSimplifier are statically instantiated. No runtime enable/disable, but future work could add rule registry.

intervention_surfaces.name: TypeStore.UsedEquivalenceClasses
intervention_surfaces.description: Type inference tracks which equivalence classes are actually used; unused classes are not emitted. No direct user override, but affects output.

intervention_surfaces.name: Program.DebugProcedureRange (debug)
intervention_surfaces.description: [DEBUG BUILD ONLY] Restrict type analysis to a range of procedures for debugging.

insights: Reko is fundamentally NOT a linear pipeline: SSA transformation contains ~15 nested mini-transforms with multiple re-runs of ValuePropagator + ConditionCodeEliminator + SsaTransform, triggered by downstream discoveries (indirect calls resolved, condition codes eliminated, stack variables found). This is a fixed-point iteration, not a sequence.

Interprocedural model via SCC processing is Reko's key differentiator: callee summaries (which registers are preserved/trashed, which parameters are used) flow UP to callers within an SCC, enabling inter-procedure optimization. This is more sophisticated than single-pass forward analysis, at the cost of re-processing each SCC until convergence.

Type reconstruction is SEPARATE from SSA: Reko doesn't infer types during SSA construction (as Ghidra does). Instead: (1) SSA builds expression trees with untyped identifiers, (2) separate type inference phase collects constraints from instructions and signatures, (3) unification happens via union-find, (4) TypedExpressionRewriter rewrites procedures with the unified types. This decoupling allows user types to constrain inference without re-running SSA.

The region structuring algorithm is iterative and sometimes unpredictable: when standard reduction rules (if/switch/sequence/loop) fail, it queues regions for refinement (virtualize edges, coalesce tails, last-resort goto insertion). It can iterate 1000+ times on complex, pathological CFGs. This is more robust than algorithms requiring perfect SESE structure, but less principled.

User annotations (signatures, globals, heuristics) flow through via Program.User, not via formal type signatures on decompilation methods. This means interventions are late-bound and scattered across many checks (e.g., 'if proc.User?.Signature, use it' appears in many places). No unified override mechanism.

Expression simplification is deeply embedded in ValuePropagator (via ExpressionSimplifier with 30+ rules). There's no way to disable specific rules or tune aggressiveness without code changes. Coalescer is separate and could be disabled.

The feedback loops are not symmetrical: SSA->ValuePropagator->SsaTransform is well-structured. But type inference has no explicit loop back to SSA; TypeTransformer can fail silently if unification discovers inconsistencies. TypeCollector is single-pass.

CFG structuring attempts to emit region-based code, but fallback 'last resort' and 'virtualize' steps can result in gotos if the input CFG is truly unstructured (e.g., irreducible loops, switch with irregular entries). This is pragmatic but means some decompiled code may have gotos despite goal to eliminate them.

The EventListener callback pattern is used for cancellation, progress, and error reporting. It does NOT support mid-stage checkpoints or phase interleaving. If a procedure fails in one stage, the whole decompilation continues; there's no per-procedure rollback.

Architecture-specific extensions (IAnalysisFactory) allow per-CPU analysis passes, but these are inserted as mini-pipelines within broader stages (AfterRegisterSsa, AfterExpressionCoalescing). No way for an architecture to inject a new top-level stage or replace a stage.
